name: Donn Cuailnge

attributes.attribute: the great Brown Bull of Cuailnge
only Irish animal to match Finnbennach the White Bull
lived in Connacht under Ailill, consort of Medb
killed Finnbennach but died of his wounds
wanted to borrow the Donn for a year to match Ailill's wealth
refused the loan after hearing Medb's men boast

sources: MacNeill, Máire. "The Festival of Lughnasa, Parts I and II." Dublin: Comhairle Bhéaloideas Éireann, 1982, 152-159.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Donn Cuailnge is an Irish mythological beast. He was the Brown Bull of Cuailnge. He was the only animal in Ireland that matched Finnbennach, the White Bull. Finnbennach lived in Ulster. His owner was the minor king Dáire. Donn Cuailnge lived in Connacht. His owner was Ailill, consort of Queen Medb. Medb and Ailill argued over who owned more. Medb found her herds had no equal to Finnbennach. She sent warriors to Dáire. She asked to borrow the Donn for a year. She offered a fortune and her own "friendly thighs." She hoped the bull would site a fine calf on one of her cows. This would make her Ailill's equal in wealth. Dáire agreed at first. Then he heard Medb's men boast. They said they would take the bull with or without his approval. Dáire grew angry and refused. This refusal started a cattle raid. The raid became the greatest of Irish epics, the Táin Bó Cuailnge. The Donn was no mere bull. He reincarnated from a man named Friuch. Friuch worked as a swineherd for the magician Bodb Derg. Another man, Rucht, worked for a man named Ochall. The two fought over everything. After they died they reincarnated in many forms. They fought as worms, stags, ravens, warriors, and phantoms. Then they became the two bulls. This shape-shifting otherwise appears only in gods and bards. Medb brought the Brown Bull to Connacht. In one pasture the bulls resumed their long combat. Donn Cuailnge killed Finnbennach. Donn Cuailnge died of his wounds soon after.

okr.objective: Records Donn Cuailnge, the Brown Bull at the center of the Táin Bó Cuailnge, and the raid his ownership began.
key_results: Donn Cuailnge was the Brown Bull, the only animal in Ireland to match Finnbennach the White Bull.
Medb arranged to borrow the bull from Dáire, hoping to equal Ailill's wealth.
Dáire's refusal, after boasting by Medb's men, began the Táin Bó Cuailnge.
The bull was the reincarnation of the swineherd Friuch.
Donn Cuailnge killed Finnbennach and died of his wounds shortly after.
